author: golden state today
title: Rep. Norma Torres addresses gender bias and accountability for powerful figures
text:
Rep. Norma Torres, a member of the U.S. Congress representing California’s 35th district, addressed issues related to gender discrimination in the military and accountability for powerful individuals in recent social media posts.
On November 17, 2025, Torres commented on gender barriers within the armed forces, stating: “Women break barriers every day. This Navy captain earned her place, yet her career was derailed because of her gender. Secretary Hegseth’s misogyny is forcing our military to work backwards.”
Later that day, she criticized the qualifications of officials serving in former President Donald Trump’s cabinet with a post reading: “Number of qualified department heads in Trumps cabinet: https://t.co/d25vNXTf7Q https://t.co/AzKycCO8VI” (November 17, 2025).
On November 18, 2025, Torres turned attention to survivors of abuse linked to high-profile figures: “The survivors of Jeffrey Epstein, Donald Trump, and other powerful predators deserve justice. No one who abuses and exploits others should be running Wall Street or making decisions in the White House. I will stand with these survivors and ensure their voices are finally heard.”
Torres has represented California’s 35th congressional district since 2015 after succeeding Gloria Negrete McLeod. Before her tenure in Congress, she served in both the California State Assembly from 2008 to 2013 and the California Senate from 2013 to 2014. Born in Escuintla, Guatemala in 1965 and currently residing in Pomona at age 58, Torres holds a Bachelor’s degree from National Labor College.
